The y-axes measure the extent to which a coref system prefers to match female pronouns with a given occupation over male pronouns, as tested by our Winogender schemas. A value of 100 (maximum female bias) means the system always resolved female pronouns to the given occupation and never male pronouns $( 1 0 0 \% - 0 \% )$ ; a score of -100 (maximum male bias) is the reverse; and a value of 0 indicates no gender differential. Recall the Winogender evaluation set is gender-balanced for each occupation; thus the horizontal dotted black line $\scriptstyle ( \mathrm { y = 0 } )$ in both plots represents a hypothetical system with $100 \%$ accuracy. Regression lines with $9 5 \%$ confidence intervals are shown.
